key_insight: A multimodal self-supervised EEG foundation model can learn generalizable seizure-related representations by aligning raw signals, time-frequency maps, and text in a shared embedding space.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve seizure detection models that transfer more reliably across datasets and support patient-independent evaluation.
method: Raw EEG encoding with a Mamba-based backbone
Time-frequency encoding with a ViT-style branch plus lightweight text encoder
Pretraining with masked modeling, cross-view contrastive alignment, and temporal consistency losses
evidence_signal: On CHB-MIT, the best single model reached AUROC 0.874 and the ensemble reached 0.878, with mean LOSO balanced accuracy of 0.558 across 19 subjects.
watch_item: Performance drops under leave-one-subject-out testing, so real-world generalization remains challenging and needs careful external validation.
paper_title: Multimodal Pretraining for Generalizable EEG Representation Learning
